brief.headline: Cut ₹28.69 L/yr excess by matching Mars Plastics price on caps and Premier Plastic on cups; we're 47.43% of their sales — plenty of room to ask.

priceAsk.summary: Match the best prices we already pay: ₹0.81/pc on the PP cap (Mars Plastics), ₹1.38/pc on the 30 mL bottle (Mars), and ₹0.35/pc on the measuring cup (Premier Plastic). That cuts our annual excess by ₹28.69 L.
priceAsk.basis: We pay Cincorp ₹1.08/pc for the 28 mm PP cap when Mars charges ₹0.81 (33.2% gap, ₹14.05 L/yr extra); ₹1.53 vs ₹1.38 on the bottle (10.7%, ₹7.88 L); and ₹0.46 vs ₹0.35 on the cup (30.6%, ₹6.75 L). The open market shows ₹0.85–0.95/pc is typical for that cap, with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so our ₹0.81 target sits comfortably in the fair band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹16.02 L of cash for us. They already take 39 days to pay their own suppliers (vs 23 days at similar firms), so they're used to longer cycles and can handle giving us a bit more time.

brief.financialLeverage: Cincorp is a small shop — ₹4.11 Cr total sales, and our ₹1.95 Cr is 47.43% of that, so we're their biggest customer by far. They keep about ₹6 of every ₹100 they sell (6.0%), half what similar firms earn (15.0%), which means price cuts hurt them more — but they also really need to keep us happy. They owe 1.13 times their own cash and sit in the grey zone for financial stress (1.83 score), so while they're not in danger today, cash is tight and they value fast payment. Push firmly on price to our best-price benchmark, then trade faster payment (which costs us ₹16.02 L in working cash but saves them ~4.54% borrowing cost) for an extra percent or two off.

evidence.point: Paying ₹28.69 L/yr more than our cheapest supplier overall
evidence.figure: ₹28.69 L total excess vs best prices we pay

evidence.point: Biggest single SKU gap: PP cap at ₹1.08 vs Mars ₹0.81
They keep less profit than rivals
They take longer to pay their own suppliers than most
Moving to 30-day terms frees up working cash for us

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; a proven, stable second source.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable; direct fit for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — perfect backup for any PET bottle SKUs.

risks: We're 47.43% of their sales — if we pull volume or push too hard on price, we could tip a small, lower-margin supplier into real trouble; line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek first so we have a credible Plan B.
They sit in the grey zone for financial stress (1.83 score) and burned ₹79.14 L in free cash last year — watch for any supply hiccups and have a backup ready to pilot one SKU.
They keep only 6.0% profit vs 15.0% at peers, so big price cuts may force quality or delivery shortcuts; tie any discount to maintaining lead times and specs.
Small entity under ₹10 Cr flagged for verification — confirm capacity, quality systems and delivery track record before locking in a long-term deal.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more per year than our best suppliers on the same items — let's close that gap and talk about how faster payment from us can help your cash flow.
